title: no verb writes a thread's title, objective, context, body or preamble -- the fourth field the typed API cannot reach
body:
**`thread.json` CARRIES `title`, `objective`, `context`, `body` AND `preamble` AS TOP-LEVEL FIELDS, AND `intent st` SHIPS NO VERB THAT WRITES ANY OF THEM.** `st` has `new start done cancel triage hold resume reopen reinstate hydrate dehydrate list show edit attach sync bootstrap`. **`st edit` only PRINTS A PATH**; `st attach` writes attachments, which these are not. So a thread's own prose is set once by `st new` and is thereafter unreachable through the typed API.

**FOUND TWICE, INDEPENDENTLY, AND THE SECOND TIME IT BLOCKED A RELEASE-SCOPE CHANGE hv HAD JUST ORDERED.** laksa-vc reported it 2026-08-31 as their D5, from the human end: hv typed an `## LLM Preamble` into a generated `info.md`, the next render dropped it (correctly -- views are projections), and the text had to be recovered from chat. **Then vc hit the same wall the same day narrowing ST0064**: hv ruled the thread narrows to the menubar app, and the title and objective still claiming the daemon's *lifecycle surface* could not be changed by any verb.

**THE ONLY ROUTE IS THE ONE THE GENERATED FOOTER ITSELF RECOMMENDS, AND IT IS THE ROUTE `0111` IS ABOUT.** *"mint or reword a row in `.canon/st/<ID>.json`, then `intent sync --to-store`"*. **Followed literally that loses the edit once the canon JSON is tracked** -- an unstaged working-tree change is not what `--to-store` reads. **The workaround that actually holds is laksa-vc's: edit the canon JSON, `git add` it, THEN `sync --to-store`** -- driven by vc on ST0064 and verified by reading the title back out of the store. **So the tool's own printed instruction is wrong for the only operation it names**, and the correct one is discoverable nowhere.

**THIS IS THE FOURTH MEMBER OF A CLASS THIS ESTATE KEEPS PAYING FOR: A FIELD THE TYPED API CANNOT REACH.** `0033` (an AT row's authored note, destroyed by a status verb), `0090` (`issues add` creates a body no verb can write), `0179` (an issue body is write-once, so a factual error in one cannot be corrected), and now every prose field on a steel thread. **The members are not related by subsystem -- they are related by the model carrying a field the surface forgot**, which is why fixing them one at a time has not stopped it recurring.

**AND THE CLASS HAS A COST THAT IS NOT THE INCONVENIENCE: IT FORCES HAND-EDITING OF CANON.** Every instance pushes an operator out of the verbs and into the JSON, which is the one path `D01` and `D34` were designed to make unnecessary, and the path every guard in the estate treats as suspicious. **A tool whose remedy for its own gap is *edit the store by hand* is training its users out of its own contract.**

**FIX.** Either a `st edit --title/--objective/--context/--body/--preamble` family, or -- better, and the shape `0179` also proposes -- **`intent edit <kind> <id> <field>` accepting the kinds the address grammar already parses**, since `address.rs` resolves `/issues/<id>` and thread ids perfectly well and the failure is only that `intent edit` maps every kind to a steel thread. **One door for *change an authored field on a modelled thing*, rather than a fifth per-subsystem verb.** Post-tag unless the tag needs another thread reworded, in which case the `git add`-then-`sync --to-store` route is the documented workaround and should be written down somewhere a reader will find it.
